S001.title: Graph Representation Learning via Causal Diffusion for Out-of-Distribution Recommendation
S001.authors: Chu Zhao; Enneng Yang; Yuliang Liang; Pengxiang Lan; Yuting Liu; Jianzhe Zhao; Guibing Guo; Xingwei Wang
S001.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Web Conference 2025
S001.arch_detail: CausalDiffRec: GNN-based recommender (LightGCN-style backbone) with causal diffusion; backdoor adjustment + variational inference for environment inference; baselines: LightGCN, SimGCL
S001.train_data_note: Datasets: Food, KuaiRec, Yelp2018, Douban; no dataset sizes reported in excerpt
S001.effect_size_notes: No effect size reported; only relative improvement percentages
S001.repr_analysis_finding: t-SNE visualization shows CausalDiffRec item embeddings of popular vs unpopular items are more evenly distributed than LightGCN's, mitigating popularity shift
S001.relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets OOD generalization failure (the sigma-trap) in GNN-based recommendation via causal diffusion and invariant learning, reporting OOD performance gains on four datasets; does not address compositional splits or training-dynamics mechanisms.
S001.relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; purely an OOD recommendation performance paper focused on invariant graph representations.
S001.other_metrics_reported: Recall@20, NDCG@20; also Recall@10/NDCG@10 in hyperparameter figures

sub_experiments.notes: Relative improvements of CausalDiffRec over LightGCN: 10.69% Food, 18.83% KuaiRec, 22.41% Yelp2018, 11.65% Douban (Recall@20/NDCG@20)

S002.venue: Proceedings of the 32nd ACM International Conference on Multimedia

S002.schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy measured; SFP prunes branches with spurious-feature dependencies but does not probe internal representations
S002.relevance_sigma_justification: Directly addresses OOD generalization failure via spurious-feature-targeted pruning for invariant substructure discovery and analyzes how highly biased data distributions hurt OOD performance, but targets correlation/domain shift rather than compositional generalization and does not connect to training dynamics or schema coherence.
S002.relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; the paper concerns OOD generalization accuracy under spurious correlations with no discussion of safety or misalignment.

S003.title: Research on Causal Robustness Enhancement Methods and Out-of-Distribution Generalization for Deep Classification Models
S003.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 6th International Conference on Computer Science and Management Technology
S003.arch_detail: ResNet-50 backbone for all methods; generative model (diffusion) for counterfactual background-replacement samples
S003.train_data_note: ImageNet-9 (background shift) and Waterbirds; no training set sizes reported
S003.augmentation_type: counterfactual data augmentation via generative foreground-preserving background replacement
S003.effect_size_notes: Paper reports approximate OOD Top-1 gains (12-16% vs standard, 6-8% vs CF-Aug) but no formal effect size; no ID accuracy reported so no gap derivable
S003.schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy; sensitivity metrics S_out/S_rep are intervention robustness, not coherence
S003.repr_analysis_finding: Measures representation/output sensitivity under background-replacement interventions: Standard S_out=0.243 S_rep=0.317, CF-Aug S_out=0.172 S_rep=0.205, CRO S_out=0.071 S_rep=0.089
S003.relevance_sigma_justification: Tests causal-robustness training against OOD/spurious-correlation failure on ImageNet-9 and Waterbirds, quantifying OOD accuracy and sensitivity to background interventions, but does not address compositional generalization or the sigma-trap structural mechanism.
S003.relevance_alignment_justification: Robustness to background/texture spurious correlations bears on reliable behavior under distribution shift, but the paper makes no explicit link to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization.
S003.limitations_text: Counterfactual quality depends on foreground-background separation and generative model accuracy, adding noise in complex scenes; causal sensitivity regularization adds computational overhead; real-world confounders are more diverse and harder to model explicitly.
S003.open_questions_text: More automated and causally interpretable counterfactual generation; extend framework to detection, segmentation, and weakly supervised or self-supervised learning.
S003.other_metrics_reported: Sensitivity metrics S_out/S_rep under background-replacement interventions

sub_experiments.notes: Full CRO (counterfactual augmentation + sensitivity regularization + invariance constraints); OOD Top-1 66.2%

CRO with lambda_inv=0 (invariance term removed); OOD Top-1 62.1%
CRO with Generation->Paste (concatenative/paste counterfactual instead of generated); OOD Top-1 61.8%

S005.title: Feature-granularity-based spurious correlation and causal analysis in CNNs Exploring Feature Granularity to Uncover Spurious Correlations
S005.venue: Proceedings of the 2024 2nd International Conference on Internet of Things and Cloud Computing Technology
S005.arch_detail: Pretrained ResNet50 classifier over 1000 ImageNet classes; analysis method = superpixel segmentation, foreground-background separation, and linear regression on superpixel features
S005.train_data_note: Uses pretrained ResNet50; ILSVRC2012 (ImageNet) validation set as sample dataset; no training described
S005.schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy; feature contributions are quantified via linear-regression coefficients, not a coherence/compositionality measure
S005.repr_analysis_finding: Identifies spurious correlations (e.g., category 'Bow tie' predicted from facial features although absent from the image); filling face/clothing regions via a generative model significantly decreased all top-3 category probabilities
S005.relevance_sigma_justification: Discusses OOD generalization failure driven by spurious correlations (facial features causing 'Bow tie' prediction) but reports no OOD experiment or accuracy numbers; interpretability/analysis method only.
S005.relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; paper targets CNN interpretability and spurious-correlation analysis for image classification deployment.
S005.limitations_text: Stresses that a sufficiently large random sample size L is crucial for robust regression coefficients; notes models relying on non-causal features generalize poorly to OOD data and face interpretability limits in regulated deployment.
S005.open_questions_text: Future work: optimize training methods to reduce reliance on non-causal features and design more interpretable, stable model frameworks for robustness on OOD data.
S005.other_metrics_reported: Linear-regression main-effect coefficients (beta) and interaction terms (rj) per superpixel block; top-3 class probabilities before/after generative inpainting

S006.open_questions_text: Open directions: compositional curricula, hybrid architecture integration, safety in adaptive systems, multi-agent compositional IL, and cognitive science synergies for lifelong adaptability.

S007.title: Don't Blind Your VLA: Aligning Visual Representations for OOD Generalization
S007.authors: Nikita Kachaev; Mikhail Kolosov; Daniil Zelezetsky; Alexey K. Kovalev; Aleksandr I. Panov
S007.venue: Proceedings of the 25th International Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems
S007.arch_detail: OpenVLA-style VLA models (pretrained VLM encoder-decoder) with action fine-tuning; vision teachers C-RADIOv3-ViT-L, DINOv2-ViT-L/G, Theia, SigLIP; normalized-sphere projection + teacher-embedding alignment
S007.train_data_note: VLA action fine-tuning; linear-probe evaluation on reduced ImageNet-100 (top-1 accuracy); OOD eval on Simpler-based benchmark
S007.schema_coherence_notes: Linear probing measures visual information retention, not a representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy
S007.repr_analysis_finding: Naive action fine-tuning degrades VLM visual representations (linear-probe top-1 accuracy on ImageNet-100 drops vs the pretrained VLM); projecting mid-level VLA features onto a normalized sphere and aligning with teacher embeddings mitigates degradation and improves OOD generalization; attention maps analyzed
S007.relevance_sigma_justification: Directly studies OOD generalization failure in VLA models: action fine-tuning degrades visual representations and generalization across Semantic/Vision/Execution axes, and visual alignment mitigates it. Does not address compositional generalization or the training-dynamics/schema-coherence mechanisms of the sigma-trap.
S007.relevance_alignment_justification: Concerns capability preservation and OOD robustness of embodied robotic agents, tangentially relevant to goal misgeneralization in agentic AI, but contains no safety, alignment, or value-learning analysis.
S007.limitations_text: Linear-probe evaluation uses a reduced ImageNet-100 due to computational constraints; probing without per-layer tuning so differences reflect representations only
S007.other_metrics_reported: task success rate per environment (mean+/-SD over 128 seeds); linear-probe top-1 accuracy (ImageNet-100)

S012.title: Causal Disentangled Recommendation against User Preference Shifts
S012.authors: Wenjie Wang; Xinyu Lin; Liuhui Wang; Fuli Feng; Yunshan Ma; Tat-Seng Chua
S012.task_custom_name: Recommendation under user preference shifts (Yelp, Book, Electronics)
S012.arch_detail: Temporal VAE; MLP encoder g_phi and decoder with FC layers f_theta1/f_lambda; learnable matrices W_z/W_x for sparse influence; hidden dims of e_t/z_t/g_phi tuned in {200,300,400}; g_phi widths [200]/[400]/[800]/[800,500]
S012.train_data_note: Three recommendation datasets (Yelp, Book, Electronics); user interaction sequences split into chronological environments; preference assumed stable within each short period
S012.schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy (probing, CKA, RSA, compositionality score) measured; KL/Euclidean analysis is a case-study alignment check, not a coherence metric
S012.repr_analysis_finding: Euclidean distance between learned user representations tracks KL divergence of category-level interaction distributions across consecutive environments, showing CDR captures preference shifts in user representations
S012.relevance_sigma_justification: Frames user preference shift as an OOD generalization problem via causal-graph environment modeling and temporal distribution shifts, but is distant from compositional generalization and the sigma-trap thesis; no treatment of training dynamics, flatness, or schema coherence.
S012.relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; the paper concerns robust recommendation quality under user preference shifts only.
S012.limitations_text: Category-level preference is non-trivial to recover from pure interaction data; performance drops when parameters grow (g_phi widened from [800] to [800,500] hurts); hidden sizes must be carefully tuned to balance representation ability and over-fitting
S012.open_questions_text: Explore more inference strategies to capture temporal patterns (current third strategy partially considers shifts but loses temporal patterns); incorporating item category into recommender models to help disentanglement

sub_experiments.notes: No quantitative main-table results in excerpt; only qualitative ablations (multi-objective loss coefficients, category number C, hidden sizes) and case study

S015.title: A.I. Robustness: a Human-Centered Perspective on Technological Challenges and Opportunities

S018.title: Abstraction Alignment: Comparing Model-Learned and Human-Encoded Conceptual Relationships

S018.arch_detail: Evaluates bert-base/large, roberta-base/large, gpt-2 on S-TEST occupation/location/birthplace specificity tasks; abstraction alignment methodology builds abstraction graphs of human concepts and measures how much model uncertainty they explain
S018.train_data_note: Pretrained LMs evaluated on S-TEST dataset; clinical coding case study uses MIMIC-III with ICD-9 codes
S018.effect_size_notes: No effect sizes or significance tests reported; quantitative results are A@10 and subgraph-preference probabilities

S018.repr_analysis_finding: Models show strong preference for specific answers when evaluated over full abstraction graphs (bert-large prefers a specific answer on over 80% of instances), contradicting prior two-answer metrics; gpt-2 has lowest accuracy/specificity but highest preference for correctness
S018.relevance_sigma_justification: Positions learned abstractions as informing a model's ability to generalize to new data, but all evaluations are in-distribution specificity benchmarks (S-TEST, ICD-9 coding); no compositional or OOD generalization measurements are made.
S018.relevance_alignment_justification: Directly targets human-AI alignment: abstraction alignment quantifies how much of a model's uncertainty is explained by human-encoded conceptual relationships, is framed against societal and regulatory alignment demands, and provides experts audit tools to locate where model behavior diverges from human abstractions; it does not, however, address goal misgeneralization or safety-critical failures.
S018.open_questions_text: Experts hypothesized abstraction alignment could improve model generation by selecting the most specific concept above a confidence threshold instead of the most probable (often overly specific and incorrect) answer; generated new hypotheses for specificity analysis.

S028.title: Data Distributional Properties As Inductive Bias for Systematic Generalization

S055.title: Compositional Generalization for Neural Semantic Parsing via Span-level Supervised Attention
S055.authors: Yin, P.; Fang, H.; Neubig, G.; Pauls, A.; Platanios, E.A.; Su, Y.; Thomson, S.; Andreas, J.
S055.venue: NAACL-HLT 2021 - 2021 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies, Proceedings of the Conference
S055.arch_detail: T5-BASE with span-level supervised attention applied to all cross-attention heads in the last decoder layer; also BERT2SEQ (BERT encoder + LSTM decoder with copy), COARSE2FINE (BERT encoder + structured sketch/value decoder), ELMO encoder + coverage-based attention seq2seq
S055.train_data_note: Semantic parsing on CFQ, SMCALFLOW-CS, ATIS; span-level alignments extracted with GIZA++ (IBM Model 4), programs canonicalized; CFQ trained on MCD splits
S055.effect_size_notes: No effect size reported; CFQ comparisons tested via p-values (bold = p <= 0.01)

S055.relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets compositional generalization failure (the sigma-trap) in semantic parsing: span-level supervised attention improves transformers, RNNs, and structured decoders on CFQ MCD, SMCALFLOW-CS, and ATIS query splits, with attention-map analysis, though it does not connect to training dynamics or schema coherence.
S055.relevance_alignment_justification: No explicit alignment or safety discussion; indirect relevance via improving robust compositional generalization of goal-directed semantic parsers used in conversational agents.
S055.limitations_text: Method struggles on CFQ conjunctive questions (discontinuous, longer/more complex aligned spans); ATIS utterance-SQL alignments noisy due to redundant SQL structures; supervision depends on external aligner (GIZA++)
S055.open_questions_text: Future work: apply span-level supervised attention to other prediction tasks and learn alignments jointly with sequence model parameters

S064.title: Grounded Graph Decoding Improves Compositional Generalization in Question Answering
S064.authors: Yu Gai; Paras Jain; Wendi Zhang; Joseph E. Gonzalez; Dawn Song; Ion Stoica
S064.arch_detail: Sequence encoder with attention + grounded graph decoder (Grounded Graph Decoding, 0.3M params); grounding attention over input retains syntax; ablations: graph decoding only and syntax-aware graph decoding; baselines LSTM+attn, Transformer, Universal Transformer, Evolved Transformer, T5, T5-11B
S064.train_data_note: CFQ benchmark; MCD1/MCD2/MCD3 splits maximize compositional divergence between train and test; main results obtained without tuning on development sets to avoid test leakage
S064.relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets compositional generalization failure (a core sigma-trap phenomenon) on CFQ MCD adversarial splits via grounded graph decoding, achieving 98.6% on MCD1, and includes an analysis of why only one syntactic composition type (conjunctive queries) limits MCD2/MCD3 performance; no connection to training dynamics or flatness.
S064.relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; purely a compositional generalization method for semantic parsing question answering.
S064.limitations_text: Grounded Graph Decoding incorporates only one type of syntactic composition (conjunctive 'A and B' queries) and cannot completely solve MCD2/MCD3; domain-specific intermediate representations (LIR/RIR) that ease the task are complex to apply to real-world datasets like CFQ; error analysis shows conjunctive structures mainly help MCD1.
S064.open_questions_text: Complement Grounded Graph Decoding with pre-training-based approaches; incorporate more complex syntactic structures beyond conjunctive queries to further boost accuracy.

S068.train_data_note: CLEVR: SPANBASEDSP trained on 10K examples vs 695K for baselines (70x less); GeoQuery small training set; SCAN-SP, CLOSURE also used
S068.effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported; headline is raw accuracy gain 61.0 -> 88.9 on compositional splits
S068.schema_coherence_notes: No internal representation-level proxy; tree F1 is output-structure faithfulness, not an internal coherence measure
S068.repr_analysis_finding: Predicted span trees vs semi-automatically annotated gold trees (F1): SCAN-SP 100 on IID/RIGHT/AROUND RIGHT; GeoQuery 94.7/91.6/93.7 (IID/TEMPLATE/LENGTH); CLEVR 70.6 on IID and CLOSURE, residual errors due to genuine ambiguity (e.g., matte block parsing)
S068.relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets the sigma-trap: documents seq2seq compositional generalization failure on GeoQuery/SCAN/CLOSURE compositional splits and shows a span-based compositional inductive bias lifts average accuracy from 61.0 to 88.9, with tree-faithfulness analysis of what is learned.
S068.relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; purely a semantic-parsing architecture and evaluation paper.
S068.limitations_text: Assumes one-to-one mapping between domain constants and their linguistic manifestations; fails where predicates do not align to phrases (e.g., text-to-SQL min/max age example); only a class of non-projective trees supported, full Corro (2020) coverage is O(n^6) and impractical.
S068.open_questions_text: Future work: introduce the explicit compositional bias inherent to SPANBASEDSP directly into seq2seq models.

S072.title: Representational Homomorphism Predicts and Improves Compositional Generalization In Transformer Language Model
S072.task_custom_name: Adapted SCAN (noise injection, primitive coverage manipulations)
S072.arch_detail: Small decoder-only Transformers trained from scratch; depth ablated 1-10 layers; layer-wise MSE-based Homomorphism Error metric using linear, bilinear, and MLP operators; no pretraining (to avoid data spoilage)
S072.train_data_note: Adapted SCAN with controlled training set primitives (1 vs 2+ primitives) and randomly inserted noise tokens (0-15)
S072.effect_size_notes: No effect size reported; effects summarized via paired t-tests (p=1.1e-4, p=0.001, p=0.023) and R2=0.73 regression
S072.schema_coherence_notes: Homomorphism Error (HE) measures deviation from compositional homomorphism between linguistic expression algebra and hidden-state space (layer-wise MSE); baseline modifier HE ~0.002 MSE at 0 noise tokens rising to ~0.012 at 15 noise; HE-regularized training significantly reduces HE (paired t-test p=1.1e-4)
S072.repr_analysis_finding: HE predicts OOD compositional generalization under noise injection (R2=0.73); model depth has minimal effect on HE or OOD accuracy; noise tokens increase modifier HE while sequence HE stays stable; HE-regularization reduces HE and improves OOD accuracy
S072.relevance_sigma_justification: Core sigma-trap study: introduces Homomorphism Error, a representation-level metric of compositional structure failure, shows it predicts OOD compositional generalization (R2=0.73), and demonstrates that regularizing HE during training significantly improves OOD accuracy (p=0.023) on an adapted SCAN benchmark.
S072.relevance_alignment_justification: Not an alignment paper, but diagnosing and controlling internal compositional structure of models (via a regularizable representational metric) is a step toward interpretability and steering relevant to understanding goal misgeneralization; no explicit safety discussion.
S072.limitations_text: Experiments on synthetic data with precisely controlled compositional structure; real-world language adds semantic ambiguity, context dependence, and irregular constructions. Evaluation on relatively small Transformer models; behavior of homomorphism error in large-scale pretrained LMs remains open.
S072.open_questions_text: Apply homomorphism error analysis to established compositional benchmarks using natural language; investigate how homomorphism error scales with model size and pretraining data; explore compositionally-aware architecture search and training procedures.
S072.other_metrics_reported: Homomorphism Error (modifier and sequence HE, layer-wise MSE averaged over linear/bilinear/MLP operators); R2 of HE-OOD accuracy regression

sub_experiments.notes: Mean OOD accuracy approximately 47% at 0 noise tokens; modifier HE ~0.002 MSE; 5 random seeds, mean and std reported

S094.relevance_sigma_justification: Directly quantifies compositional generalization failure in pretrained T5: under controlled lexical exposure (novel character sequences and novel-embedding tokens) COGS generalization drops from 83% to 6-32%, exposing pretraining-data leakage as the cause of overestimated compositional generalization and demonstrating inverse scaling with pretraining corpus size; central to the sigma-trap diagnosis.
S094.relevance_alignment_justification: Concerns overestimation of generalization performance in pretrained models due to evaluation leakage, bearing on trustworthy capability assessment of foundation models, but it does not discuss alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization directly.

S095.title: A Neuroscience-Inspired Dual-Process Model of Compositional Generalization
S095.authors: Alex Noviello; Claas Beger; Jacob Groner; Kevin Ellis; Weinan Sun
S095.arch_detail: MIRAGE dual-process model: System 1 = meta-trained Transformer Neural Decomposer (single-step compositional decomposition); System 2 = Schema Engine (rule-based, prioritized schemas, episodic bindings); iterative refinement loop; baselines: vanilla Transformer and Transformer+SC_Library prompt
S095.train_data_note: System 1 meta-trained to perform single-step decomposition on a stream of random grammars; evaluated task-agnostically (zero-shot) on all SCAN splits
S095.schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy measured; the schema library is symbolic and interpretability is discussed qualitatively via stepwise traces
S095.relevance_sigma_justification: Directly confronts the sigma-trap: systematic compositional generalization failure in deep learning. MIRAGE achieves >99% accuracy on all SCAN splits (including Length, Add prim, Template designed to foil seq2seq models) via a dual-process neuro-inspired architecture, with ablations isolating schema priorities, iterative refinement, and accurate schemas as causes of systematic behavior; offers a processing and interpretability account of why compositional failure occurs and how it can be overcome.
S095.relevance_alignment_justification: Not an alignment/safety paper, but its externalized, stepwise-verifiable schema traces and cognitive-architecture framing speak to interpretability and transparency concerns that are adjacent to AI safety; no direct treatment of goal misgeneralization.
S095.limitations_text: MIRAGE relies on reliable extraction of a consistent grammar; robustness to noisy or incomplete schemas is not yet addressed; evaluation is limited to SCAN.
S095.open_questions_text: Extend the schema extractor with probabilistic rule learning and active retrieval for noisy schemas; apply the architecture to more complex reasoning tasks; use its inspectable states to test neuroscientific hypotheses about HPC-PFC interactions during planning.

S096.title: Compositional generalization in a deep seq2seq model by separating syntax and semantics
S096.authors: Jake Russin; Jason Jo; Randall C. O'Reilly; Yoshua Bengio
S096.arch_detail: Syntactic Attention: seq2seq NMT (Bahdanau attention setup) with separate syntactic and semantic attention heads, inspired by distinct neural systems for syntax and semantics; no hand-engineered features or extra supervision
S096.train_data_note: SCAN; add-jump split (jump held out except basic context, up to 32 added jump commands in scaling experiment); template splits: jump around right, primitive right, primitive opposite right, primitive around right
S096.effect_size_notes: No effect size reported; mean accuracies with SDs across random samples
S096.schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy measured; attention visualizations are qualitative, not a scalar coherence metric
S096.repr_analysis_finding: Attention visualizations (Figures 10-15) show the model applies the same syntactic rules learned on other verbs to the novel verb 'jump' on test examples; failure mode occurs when the model fails to attend to the correct sequence of commands
S096.relevance_sigma_justification: Directly studies compositional generalization failure on SCAN add-jump and template splits, showing RNN seq2seq models fail catastrophically (12.5%) while the syntax/semantics-separated Syntactic Attention nearly solves it, with attention analyses of the underlying mechanism - squarely a sigma-trap investigation.
S096.relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; a cognitive-science-inspired seq2seq architecture paper with no safety discussion.
S096.limitations_text: Syntactic Attention fails on Primitive opposite right (10.5%) and Primitive around right (28.9%) template splits where the left-right symmetry is violated; attention mechanism sometimes fails to attend to the correct command sequence
S096.open_questions_text: Further research required on whether a model implementing similar principles can perform well on template splits where the symmetry between left and right is violated
S096.other_metrics_reported: Mean accuracy (%) with SD over 5 random samples; attention weight visualizations

S098.title: Learning to Recombine and Resample Data for Compositional Generalization
S098.authors: Ekin Akyürek; Afra Feyza Akyürek; Jacob Andreas

S099.title: Can Transformers Jump Around Right in Natural Language? Assessing Performance Transfer from SCAN
S099.authors: Rahma Chaabouni; Roberto Dessì; Eugene Kharitonov
S099.arch_detail: Vanilla Transformer with focused modifications: SAG (relative-position attention graph), convolution self-attention, fixed span, T5-style local attention with learned relative-position bias; fairseq setup with encoder/decoder normalize-before; ConvS2S-inspired localization
S099.train_data_note: SCAN splits (jump etc.); low-resource FLoRes MT (ne-en, si-en, en-ne, en-si); newly introduced distribution-shifted compositional English-French translation task; noun-adjective order agreement dataset
S099.effect_size_notes: No formal effect sizes; relative gains reported (13.1% BLEU low-resource, 14% COMP, 1.44% noun-adjective)
S099.repr_analysis_finding: Softmaxed learned relative-position biases (bij) show many heads strongly prefer fixed local positions; several heads dominantly attend to particular positions; local attention linked to SCAN compositional generalization; some heads retain ability to look beyond span, explaining T5's edge over fixed-span
S099.repr_analysis_layer: all encoder/decoder layers, e.g. encoder layer 0 head 7, layer 2 heads 3,7; decoder layer 2 heads 3,4,5
S099.relevance_sigma_justification: Directly investigates compositional generalization on SCAN, shows Transformer variants with localized attention (SAG+T5) jump from near-zero to ~60% SCAN-jump accuracy, and tests whether this capability transfers to low-resource and distribution-shifted MT — a direct empirical probe of when comp-gen competence matters.
S099.relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; a transfer/architecture analysis across SCAN and machine translation.
S099.other_metrics_reported: BLEU on FLoRes dev-test (ne-en 8.40+/-0.02 vs Transformer 7.94+/-0.05 for SAG+T5; en-ne 5.01+/-0.10 vs 4.43+/-0.01) and on compositional En-Fr (41.43+/-0.29 vs 40.86+/-0.34); sig at p<1e-3 and p<0.05 respectively; noun-adjective SAG +1.44% relative

S100.title: Learning to Generalize Compositionally by Transferring Across Semantic Parsing Tasks
S100.authors: Wang Zhu; Peter Shaw; Tal Linzen; Fei Sha
S100.arch_detail: DUEL algorithm: encoder and task-specific decoder layers trained on different compositional splits during pre-finetuning, then fine-tuned on the target task; encoder-decoder models T5-Base and BERT2SEQ (BERT encoder + seq2seq decoder)

S100.effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported; comparisons reported as exact-match percentages (e.g., 57.8% GEO TMCD with SCAN cd pre-finetuning vs 56.6% NQG-T5)
S100.schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy measured; the encoder is argued to acquire a transferable inductive bias, but no probing or coherence metric is reported
S100.relevance_sigma_justification: Directly addresses compositional generalization failure by transferring a compositional inductive bias across semantic parsing tasks (COGS, GeoQuery, SCAN); DUEL with compositional-split pre-finetuning surpasses the prior hybrid SotA on GeoQuery TMCD with a purely neural model, with ablations characterizing each step.
S100.relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; framed purely as improving compositional generalization via transfer learning in semantic parsing.
S100.limitations_extractor: No limitations section present in excerpt; COGS structural generalization noted as 'too difficult for purely neural models, even with DUEL'
S100.open_questions_text: Future research: investigate why same-type compositional pre-finetuning splits yield only minor improvements on COGS structural generalization (4.5% to 5.2%) and develop approaches for extracting a stronger inductive bias.

S101.title: Compositional generalization in semantic parsing with pretrained transformers
S101.arch_detail: T5-base and T5-3b fine-tuned on SCAN/COGS; pretraining domains varied: C4 (English), non-English corpora (marian), CodeT5 (programming languages), protein sequence modeling (pt5 base/xl)
S101.train_data_note: SCAN and COGS, relatively small English datasets; models trained to convergence; average generalization accuracy over splits reported
S101.effect_size_notes: No effect sizes; gains quoted as absolute percentage-point improvements (e.g., ~23% and ~73% absolute in SCAN from C4 pretraining)
S101.schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence or compositionality proxy; analysis is behavioral (downstream generalization accuracy)
S101.relevance_sigma_justification: Directly quantifies compositional generalization failure on SCAN and COGS as a function of pretraining domain and model scale, showing pretraining (especially for larger models) narrows the OOD gap, but the study is behavioral with no mechanism, training-dynamics, or representation-level analysis of the sigma-trap.
S101.relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; the work is about pretraining transfer for semantic parsing.
S101.open_questions_text: Whether the content-specificity conditions for successful transfer can be delineated; whether pretraining generalization benefits are explainable by content-independent modifications (embedding scale, relative position sensitivity); whether transfer tasks should be more challenging (zero-shot/few-shot) to reveal pretrained knowledge.

S102.title: CNNs found to jump around more skillfully than RNNs: Compositional generalization in seq2seq convolutional networks
S102.arch_detail: Out-of-the-box fairseq convolutional seq2seq: multi-layer CNN encoder-decoder with multi-layer attention; hyperparameter search over learning rate, layer dimensionality (128-512), layer count (6-10), kernel width (3-5), dropout (0-0.5)
S102.train_data_note: SCAN splits: random (80/20), jump, around-right, length, turn-left; CNN tested on random, jump and around-right (length near 0%, turn-left near-perfect)
S102.effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported; comparisons are descriptive mean accuracies across seeds
S102.schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy measured; error analyses are behavioral, not representational
S102.relevance_sigma_justification: Directly measures compositional generalization failure (the sigma-trap) on SCAN's jump and around-right splits, showing a CNN far outperforms RNNs, and analyzes kernel width, multi-layer attention, and error structure to explain why the CNN still does not induce systematic compositional rules.
S102.relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; the paper is an architecture comparison on a compositional generalization benchmark.
S102.limitations_text: CNN's learned positional embeddings do not generalize beyond training lengths (length split near 0%); shallow CNNs cannot handle even the random split; self-attentive networks left untested as more cumbersome to train; CNN induces no rule-like systematicity; best LSTM has 1/4 the parameters of the best CNN.
S102.open_questions_text: Future work: investigate which CNN aspects (kernel width, multi-layer attention) are crucial for compositional generalization; formulate a tighter CNN vs LSTM comparison under matched depth and parameter budgets.
S102.other_metrics_reported: error proportions across command words; output-length error variance under kernel-width variation; attention-layer ablation accuracies

S104.title: On graph-based reentrancy-free semantic parsing
S104.arch_detail: Graph-based span parser: CYK/ILP MAP inference with grammar constraints, constraint smoothing + conditional gradient solver; ~5 sentences/sec on GeoQuery; baselines: seq2seq, BERT2SEQ, BART, span-based SP
S104.train_data_note: SCAN, GeoQuery, CLEVR standard splits: IID plus compositional splits (RIGHT, ARIGHT, TEMPLATE, LENGTH, CLOSURE); weakly-supervised latent tag anchoring discussed; dataset sizes not in excerpt

S104.relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; a semantic parsing methodology paper with complexity proofs and benchmark evaluations.

S104.open_questions_text: Extensions for ASTs containing reentrancies; cases where a single word anchors more than one predicate or entity; more general research on neural architectures that generalize better to longer sentences.

S105.title: LAGr: Labeling Aligned Graphs for Improving Systematic Generalization in Semantic Parsing
S105.arch_detail: LAGr graph-labeling parser: predicts node and edge labels for a multi-layer input-aligned graph using a shared Transformer encoder; PED (positional embedding downscaling) init; weakly-supervised variant with approximate MAP alignment via Hungarian matching (K candidates, noise sigma)
S105.train_data_note: CFQ MCD1/MCD2/MCD3 splits + random split (used as in-distribution for tuning); COGS train/gen sets. Metric is graph accuracy (predicted vs true graph isomorphism), comparable to exact-match accuracy of prior work
S105.schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy; LAGr changes output structure (graph labeling), not internal representations
S105.relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets compositional generalization failure (the sigma-trap) on COGS and CFQ: LAGr graph-labeling raises CFQ MCD mean from ~18% seq2seq baselines to ~39% and beats all baselines on every MCD split, but does not study training dynamics, flatness, or representation-level schema coherence.
S105.relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; a semantic-parsing method paper concerned only with compositional accuracy.
S105.limitations_text: Weakly-supervised LAGr does not always converge on the training set; runs not reaching 99.5% training graph accuracy (~12%) were discarded. Duplicate node labels in 3.7-5.7% of CFQ examples complicate alignment inference (fixes 2.7% hard article cases via cached alignment candidate). Lexicons not integrated.
S105.open_questions_text: Future work: modify LAGr to condition edge predictions on node labels (based on error analysis); use a pretrained encoder; apply more advanced discrete optimization or amortized inference methods for alignment; lexicons can be integrated though not expected to help on COGS.

S106.title: ReCOGS: How Incidental Details of a Logical Form Overshadow an Evaluation of Semantic Interpretation

S111.title: Inducing Transformer's Compositional Generalization Ability via Auxiliary Sequence Prediction Tasks

S116.title: Does Data Scaling Lead to Visual Compositional Generalization?
S116.authors: Arnas Uselis; Andrea Dittadi; Seong Joon Oh
S116.task_custom_name: Controlled concept-combination benchmarks: PUG Shapes3D, dSprites, FunnySprites (introduced), Colored-MNIST, MPI3D
S116.arch_detail: ResNet-50 trained from scratch as primary baseline; comparisons with ViT (patch 8/16, depth 4-8, width 384-512, heads 8/12, MLP 384-512); pretrained DINOv2 ViT-L, DINOv1 ResNet-50, DINO ViT-L, CLIP ViT-L; linear and 2-layer MLP [512,512] probes

S116.relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; concerns vision-model compositional accuracy and dataset design only.
S116.open_questions_text: Motivates stronger emphasis on constructing diverse datasets for compositional generalization and on representational structure that enables efficient compositional learning; notes partial presence of factored structure in pretrained models (DINO, CLIP) warranting further study.

S119.title: Learning to Think in Physics: Breaking Shortcut Learning in Scientific Diffusion via Representation Alignment
S119.authors: Haozhe Jia; Pengyu Yin; Wenshuo Chen; Shaofeng Liang; Lei Wang; Bowen Tian; Xiucheng Wang; Nanqian Jia; Yutao Yue
S119.task_custom_name: PDE generation: Darcy flow, topology optimization, electrostatic potential, turbulent channel flow
S119.arch_detail: Physics-informed diffusion model (REPA-P) on U-Net and Diffusion Transformer (DiT) backbones; lightweight 1x1 projection heads decode hidden activations to physical states with PDE residual losses during training
S119.train_data_note: Four PDE tasks (Darcy flow, topology optimization, electrostatic potential, turbulent channel flow); Darcy training runs 120K iterations; no dataset sizes in excerpt
S119.effect_size_notes: Metrics are physics residuals, data losses, PSNR, and compliance errors (lower-is-better); no accuracy-style effect sizes reported
S119.schema_coherence_proxy_other: physical decodability (1x1 projection heads decode hidden activations to PDE state variables)
S119.schema_coherence_notes: REPA-P aligns intermediate diffusion features with physical states via projection heads and PDE residual losses; Figure 5 shows 47%-100% physics residual reduction across U-Net layers vs output-only physics loss
S119.repr_analysis_finding: Intermediate features are decodable to physical quantities (Physical Decodability); bottleneck alignment best, 47%-100% physics residual reduction vs output-only alignment; heads discarded at inference with zero overhead

S131.title: Diagnosing Generalization Failures from Representational Geometry Markers
S131.authors: Chi-Ning Chou; Artem Kirsanov; Yao-Yuan Yang; SueYeon Chung
S131.task_custom_name: OOD transfer learning to 9 datasets: Flowers102, Stanford Cars, Places365, Food101, Oxford-IIIT Pet, etc. (linear probe test accuracy)
S131.arch_detail: 20 popular ImageNet-pretrained architectures from PyTorch official repository, each with two weight sets (v1/v2); exploratory experiments across diverse architectures, optimizers, and datasets
S131.train_data_note: ImageNet-pretrained models (weights from PyTorch hub); v2 weights achieve higher ImageNet ID accuracy than v1; OOD transfer evaluated with linear probes on 9 downstream datasets
S131.effect_size_notes: Derived: marker-based OOD-transfer prediction accuracy 73.02% minus ID-accuracy-based prediction 37.22% = +0.358 raw delta in prediction accuracy (92/126 correct predictions vs ID-accuracy baseline)
S131.schema_coherence_notes: Prognostic markers are ID object-manifold geometry: effective manifold dimensionality (Deff) and utility (Psi_eff); reduced values (overcompression) predict weaker OOD generalization and overspecialization. No numeric marker values reported in excerpt; effective_rank used as closest vocabulary proxy for Deff
S131.repr_analysis_finding: Object-manifold geometry analysis: low effective manifold dimensionality (Deff) and utility (Psi_eff) of ID representations forecast poor OOD generalization; with comparable ID validation accuracy, larger Deff/Psi_eff reflect richer task-relevant variability while excessive compression signals ID overspecialization; geometry predicted v1>v2 OOD transfer in 14/20 architectures despite v2's higher ID accuracy
S131.relevance_sigma_justification: Directly addresses anticipating OOD generalization failure: shows overcompression of ID object manifolds (low Deff/Psi_eff) predicts weaker OOD performance across diverse architectures, optimizers, and datasets, and beats ID accuracy as a transfer model-selection signal; a diagnostic biomarker framework for the sigma-trap, though not about compositional structure or training dynamics.
S131.relevance_alignment_justification: Implicitly supports safe deployment by predicting OOD failures and improving model selection, and frames diagnostics as a complement to mechanistic interpretability for anticipating vulnerabilities, but contains no direct discussion of alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization.
S131.open_questions_text: Strengthening theoretical foundations linking manifold overcompression to feature overspecialization; causal mechanisms and interventions (geometry-aware regularization, early stopping, robustness-oriented model selection); extending the diagnostic framework beyond vision to language, RL, and multimodal models; linking diagnostics to parameter transfer (Net2Net); parallels with neuroscience.
S131.other_metrics_reported: Prognostic-marker prediction accuracy 73.02% (92/126) vs 37.22% for ID test accuracy as OOD-performance predictor, across 15 models x 9 OOD datasets; Neural Collapse and Participation Ratio markers also predictive; early fine-tuning dynamics differ by initialization (v1 sometimes faster learning)

S138.title: Navigating High Dimensional Concept Space with Metalearning
S138.task_custom_name: Few-shot Boolean concept classification from PCFG-generated logical statements

S144.title: Improving Latent Generalization Using Test-time Compute
S144.authors: Arslan Chaudhry; Sridhar Thiagarajan; Andrew Lampinen
S144.task_custom_name: Latent generalization: syllogism, reversal (strict/non-strict), category-as-subject/target fact recall
S144.arch_detail: Finetuned decoder-only language model (exact model not named in excerpt); trained via RL from correctness feedback to produce long chain-of-thought (thinking); ICL condition as reference
S144.train_data_note: Knowledge finetuning tasks (syllogisms, reversal facts, category-subject/target facts); OOD = holdout knowledge not trained on (no RL performed on it)
S144.train_regime_other: Reinforcement learning from correctness feedback for long chain-of-thought (thinking)
S144.augmentation_type: Train-time data augmentation (e.g., strings in forward and reverse directions); Augmentation and Augmentation+RL baselines
S144.effect_size_notes: Qualitative claims (thinking resolves many latent generalization failures; above-chance on reversal via generate-and-verify; below ICL) without extractable effect sizes.
S144.schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy measured; only behavioral accuracy metrics.
S144.relevance_sigma_justification: Directly studies a generalization failure mode of finetuned LMs (latent generalization deficit, including the reversal curse) where in-weights knowledge fails to compose into logically implied OOD queries, and tests whether test-time thinking with RL-from-correctness closes the OOD gap versus augmentation baselines that fail OOD, though training sharpness and schema coherence are not examined.
S144.relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; the work targets capability (deductive reasoning over in-weights knowledge) with no alignment or risk discussion.
S144.other_metrics_reported: All F1, Train Recall, Heldout Recall, Primary Reference In Prediction, Pass@1 and Pass@16 at N=1 and N=16 (best-of-n sampling); thinking consistently outperforms Finetuning+RL and Augmentation+RL baselines, often matching ICL on ID and OOD; augmentation fails to generalize OOD similarly to plain finetuning; on pure reversal tasks thinking remains below ICL.

S148.title: Predictable GRPO: A Closed-Form Model of Training Dynamics
S148.authors: Rajat Ghosh; Datta Nimmaturi; Aryan Singhal; Vaishnavi Bhargava; Henry Wong; Johnu George; Debojyoti Dutta
S148.task_custom_name: GRPO RL post-training on GSM8K; OOD eval on 8 math benchmarks (GSM-Plus, Math-500, AIME-2026, MetaMathQA, NuminaMath, OpenMath2, IMO-Bench, HMMT-2025)
S148.arch_detail: GRPO RL post-training (LoRA rank 16, alpha 64) of decoder-only LLMs DeepSeek-7B, DeepSeek-R1-Qwen-1.5B, Nemotron-4B; paper's contribution is a closed-form reduced-order (stochastically-forced damped oscillator) model of GRPO training dynamics
S148.train_data_note: GRPO on GSM8K; config: LR 1e-5, 2 epochs, batch size 4 (grad accum 4), temperature 0.8, KL beta 0.005, clip 0.2, LoRA r=16 alpha=64 on q,k,v,o,up,down,gate; OOD eval on 8 math benchmarks (pass@k)
S148.train_regime_other: GRPO (group relative policy optimization) reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards; heavy-ball optimizer with momentum
S148.effect_size_notes: No effect sizes; key quantitative claim is closed-form trajectory fitting training reward to R2>=0.91 and group-size invariance of the mean trajectory (OOD transfer to eight math benchmarks)
S148.schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy; analysis is of training reward dynamics, not internal representations
S148.relevance_sigma_justification: Studies GRPO training dynamics via closed-form reduced-order modeling with OOD evaluation on eight math benchmarks, but its focus is optimizer dynamics and reward scaling laws rather than compositional or OOD generalization failure mechanisms.
S148.relevance_alignment_justification: Provides diagnostics that separate reward hacking, advantage degeneracy, and policy concentration in RL post-training of LLMs — failure modes directly relevant to reward misalignment in RLHF-style training; scope is mechanism and scaling, with no treatment of AGI safety or goal misgeneralization.
S148.limitations_text: Stability threshold and overdamped-to-oscillatory transition only exercised in a softmax-bandit exact reduction (deep-network demonstration left to future work); reduction is local (linearization at fixed point) so it describes approach to saturation, not the global trajectory; curvature-scaling exponent K(M) inherited from empirical fits, not derived; within-group reward spread retains residual group-size dependence.
S148.open_questions_text: Deep-network demonstration of the stability sweep; a model of residual group-size structure in within-group spread sigma_adv; treatment of the pre-linear phase; relating the fitted curvature-scaling exponent to lazy/NTK-regime slowdown to convert it into a predicted exponent.
S148.other_metrics_reported: Closed-form fit R2>=0.91 to training reward; pass@1/pass@5 on 8 OOD math benchmarks; stability threshold K*eta*Kref>1-mu (Proposition 9); refresh-interval stability threshold; 1/G stationary fluctuation scaling; group-size invariance of mean trajectory

S149.title: Can Large Reasoning Models do Analogical Reasoning under Perceptual Uncertainty?
S149.authors: Giacomo Camposampiero; Michael Hersche; Roger Wattenhofer; Abu Sebastian; Abbas Rahimi
S149.task_custom_name: I-RAVEN / I-RAVEN-X analogical reasoning (Raven's progressive matrices, symbolic)
S149.arch_detail: Large Reasoning Models (OpenAI o3-mini, DeepSeek R1) with test-time compute scaling; neuro-symbolic probabilistic abductive model ARLC (VSA-based) with entropy regularization
S149.train_data_note: Symbolic I-RAVEN and I-RAVEN-X puzzles (10 panels per row vs 3, up to 100x more attribute values); I-RAVEN-X extended with confounding attributes and smoothened attribute distributions; no dataset sizes in excerpt
S149.train_regime_other: no training for LRMs (prompting with test-time reasoning); ARLC trained with entropy-regularized probabilistic abduction
S149.effect_size_notes: Paper directly reports 'o3-mini loses up to 69.6% accuracy' from standard I-RAVEN to I-RAVEN-X with uncertainty; converted from percentage to proportion
S149.relevance_sigma_justification: Directly quantifies OOD/compositional generalization failure in large reasoning models: extending reasoning rules (I-RAVEN to I-RAVEN-X) plus perceptual uncertainty collapses o3-mini from 86.6% to 17.0% and R1 from 80.6% to 23.2% (near chance), while a neuro-symbolic model stays at 88.0% - a sharp quantitative demonstration of the generalization failure at the heart of the sigma-trap, though the uncertainty manipulation is synthetic.
S149.relevance_alignment_justification: No explicit alignment framing; relevance is indirect through reliability of large reasoning models under OOD conditions, which matters for trustworthy deployment, but the paper does not discuss safety, goal misgeneralization, or alignment mechanisms.
S149.limitations_text: Three-bin discretization oversimplifies real perception modules which would distribute uncertainty more broadly; encoding uncertainty yields longer and less efficient LRM prompts that may impair reasoning; unimodal nature of LLMs/LRMs constrains evaluation to purely symbolic datasets, not extended to the visual domain
S149.open_questions_text: Open-domain robust analogical reasoning models remain a mirage and need future investment; more thorough investigation of the simulated perceptual-uncertainty limitations is left to future work
S149.other_metrics_reported: Reasoning tokens for o3-mini: 7209 (base) -> 18,589 (combined noise), 53,596 at high reasoning effort (accuracy 31.0%); arithmetic reasoning gains up to 65.4% for LRMs; random chance accuracy 12.5%; ARLC Pareto-frontier accuracy-cost scaling vs o3-mini

S150.title: Compositional Generalization via Semantic Tagging
S150.task_custom_name: Also ATIS and WikiSQL subset (not in vocabulary); semantic parsing to lambda-calculus and SQL
S150.arch_detail: Two-stage decoding: input first tagged with semantic symbols, then seq2seq parser generates meaning representation conditioning on utterance and tag sequence; base seq2seq archs: Transformer, LSTM, RoBERTa; ST = semantic tagging, AS = attention supervision
S150.train_data_note: GeoQuery (lambda-calculus and SQL), ATIS (lambda-calculus and SQL), WikiSQL subset; question-based vs query-based splits; results averaged over 5 random seeds
S150.train_regime_other: two-stage decoding with semantic tagging (ST); attention supervision (AS) variant; GECA baseline uses data augmentation
S150.effect_size_notes: No effect size; absolute-point gains reported descriptively (6.2 on ATIS lambda, 10.8 on GeoQuery SQL over RoBERTa)
S150.schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy; semantic tagger is a task-level decoding component (per-word semantic symbol prediction), not a representation analysis
S150.relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets compositional generalization failure (sigma-trap): standard seq2seq semantic parsers fail on unseen compositions of seen components, and the semantic-tagging two-stage decoding framework improves compositional generalization across architectures (Transformer, LSTM, RoBERTa) and semantic formalisms, though it still fails on unseen syntactic structure.
S150.relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; purely a natural language semantic parsing methodology paper.
S150.limitations_text: Semantic tagging requires alignments between linguistic expressions and atomic semantic symbols; gains are limited on ATIS SQL due to bridging columns that do not align with any linguistic expression, and the method fails to generalize to unseen compositions of seen syntactic structures (e.g., Cats like fish that like water).
S150.open_questions_text: How to automatically select appropriate symbols as semantic tags is left for future work; the authors would like to extend the approach to learning syntactic generalizations.

S151.arch_detail: Edge Transformer: Transformer variant with 3D tensor edge states (vector per pair of input nodes) and triangular attention inspired by unification in logic programming, O(n^3) complexity; encoder-decoder version for CFQ semantic parsing; graph version for COGS; baselines: Universal Transformer, vanilla Transformer, Relation-aware Transformer, BiLSTM, LSTM+Lex, T5-small

S152.title: Compositional Generalization from First Principles
S152.authors: Thaddäus Wiedemer; Prasanna Mayilvahanan; Matthias Bethge; Wieland Brendel
S152.task_custom_name: synthetic sprite-image reconstruction from latent factors (5-d component latents mapped to 64x64 RGB images)

S152.relevance_sigma_justification: Foundational theoretical treatment of compositional generalization: derives sufficient conditions (compositional support, sufficient support, non-collapsed composition) on training support and architecture under which compositional generalization provably occurs, targeting exactly the sigma-trap failure observed even in models with explicit compositional priors; empirically shows failure localizes precisely where conditions are violated.

S152.open_questions_text: Extend to unsupervised identifiable representation learning; relax the initial-point condition via a self-consistency condition; learn unknown composition functions; extend error bounds beyond perfect training fit; relax conditions using inductive biases such as shift invariance.

S177.title: When does compositional structure yield compositional generalization? A kernel theory
S177.task_custom_name: symbolic addition; context dependence; transitive equivalence/ordering (compositional toy tasks)
S177.arch_detail: Kernel models with fixed, compositionally structured representations (theory object); empirical validation on convolutional networks, residual networks, and Vision Transformers; salience analysis of random-weight networks (0-20 layers, step/ReLU/leaky ReLU/rectified quadratic/Gaussian nonlinearities)
S177.train_data_note: Compositional tasks built from component conjunctions (symbolic addition, context dependence, transitive equivalence/ordering); DSprites disentangled-representation models in appendix
S177.effect_size_notes: No effect sizes or quantitative accuracy results reported in the excerpt
S177.schema_coherence_notes: Introduces representational salience S(k;C), a normalized metric of how strongly each component conjunction is encoded in the representation (computed from kernel similarities); analyzed qualitatively across depth and nonlinearity (Fig. 3), no numeric values given in the excerpt
S177.repr_analysis_finding: Representational salience analysis shows deep random ReLU networks increasingly encode only the full conjunction (S(C;C) approaches 1 with depth), so very deep networks implement a look-up table memorizing training data without generalizing to novel component combinations; moderately conjunctive representations still suffer memorization leak and shortcut bias.
S177.relevance_sigma_justification: Provides a formal kernel theory of when compositional structure fails to yield compositional generalization (the sigma-trap): it proves compositionally structured kernel models are restricted to conjunction-wise additive functions, identifies two concrete failure modes (memorization leak and shortcut bias) driven by training-data statistics, and shows when very deep networks memorize rather than generalize; relevance tempered by the absence of benchmark-scale empirical results in the excerpt.
S177.relevance_alignment_justification: No direct treatment of AI alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; relevance is indirect via understanding and remedying compositional generalization failure modes in deep learning models, which bears on dependable generalization.
S177.limitations_text: Theory is restricted to kernel models with fixed, compositionally structured representations (treated as the best-case scenario for compositional generalization); extension to randomly sampled or learned representations is a conjecture with preliminary evidence (in expectation, and empirically on DSprites in the appendix).
S177.open_questions_text: Whether learned disentangled representations are useful for downstream compositional generalization remains unclear; framework grounds research into learning mechanisms that implement compositional computations other than conjunction-wise additivity, and helps design hard benchmark tasks not solvable by kernel models.

S187.title: Layer-wise Representation Fusion for Compositional Generalization
S187.authors: Yafang Zheng; Lei Lin; Shuangtao Li; Yuxuan Yuan; Zhaohong Lai; Shan Liu; Biao Fu; Yidong Chen; Xiaodong Shi
S187.arch_detail: Seq2seq Transformer (6 encoder + 6 decoder layers); LRF adds a fuse-attention module at each encoder and decoder layer (~12M extra parameters); variants LRF-Small, LRF-Rela, LRF-onlytop, Transformer-accu; RoBERTa-based and HPD baselines
S187.train_data_note: CFQ with MCD splits (MCD1-3); CoGnition German translation dataset with CG-test set; results averaged over 3 random runs
S187.effect_size_notes: No formal effect sizes; improvements reported as raw percentage-point deltas (e.g., -8.4% CTERInst, -12.6% CTERAggr, ~21% relative EM improvement over RoBERTa)
S187.schema_coherence_notes: Representation entanglement (RE) is discussed as the failure cause and analyzed via attention visualizations, but no representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy metric is reported
S187.repr_analysis_finding: Visualization of fuse-attention probabilities per layer shows LRF learns layer-specific fusion weights (e.g., lower layers concentrate on a few prior layers while higher layers attend more broadly), supporting the claim that shallow residual connections under-fuse earlier-layer information and cause representation entanglement; encoder-side fusion helps more than decoder-side.
S187.repr_analysis_layer: fuse-attention modules at each of the 6 encoder and 6 decoder layers
S187.relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets compositional generalization failure (the sigma-trap): proposes LRF to fix representation entanglement in seq2seq Transformers, diagnoses the mechanism (shallow residual connections causing information forgetting and entanglement), and evaluates on CFQ MCD splits and CoGnition CG-test with clear quantitative gains (CFQ MCD-mean 43.4 -> 52.4; CTER -8.4% instance-level); relevance limited by its single-method focus and lack of training-dynamics or schema-coherence measurements.
S187.relevance_alignment_justification: No direct connection to AI alignment or goal misgeneralization; relevance is indirect through improving compositional generalization, a capability related to robust generalization of deployed language models.
S187.limitations_text: Improvements on CoGnition are moderate and LRF is worse than Dangle there, attributed to natural-language compositionality being more complex than rigid arithmetic-like operations; LRF adds ~12M parameters; task-optimized HPD still outperforms LRF on CFQ; simple accumulation (Transformer-accu) hurts performance.
S187.other_metrics_reported: CTER (compatibility test error rate, instance- and aggregate-level) on CoGnition CG-test; fuse-attention probability visualizations

S188.title: Block-Operations: Using Modular Routing to Improve Compositional Generalization
S188.task_custom_name: Synthetic algorithmic tasks (double-addition, logical rules/variable assignment); BPMNIST (block-permuted MNIST)
S188.arch_detail: SMFR = Stack of Multiplexers and FNNs with gated residual connections implementing modular representation-preserving mappings (block-operations); Multiplexer enhances the FNN; grid sizes ~20k-500k params; BPMNIST ~4M params
S188.train_data_note: Synthetic algorithmic task (double-addition) with OOD even/odd iterations; BPMNIST with 8 block permutations, one number held out per test permutation

S188.schema_coherence_notes: No coherence proxy scored; modularity assessed qualitatively via routing-weight inspection and attention indicators

S188.relevance_sigma_justification: Directly addresses the sigma-trap by attributing compositional generalization failure to static routing in neural networks; shows FNNs and Transformers only learn heuristic approximations while the SMFR learns the underlying atomic operations and generalizes perfectly OOD on algorithmic tasks.
S188.relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; an architecture-level generalization paper.

S188.open_questions_text: Use the principles of block-operations to improve other existing architectures (future work)
S188.other_metrics_reported: OODeven/OODodd accuracy by model-size category (Table 7); OOD accuracy over training (convergence behavior); attention sharpness, permutation-undoing, and attention fairness indicators on BPMNIST

S189.title: Local Mechanisms of Compositional Generalization in Conditional Diffusion
S189.task_custom_name: CLEVR conditional diffusion (location- and color-conditioned image generation)
S189.ood_difficulty_metric_name: Kmax (max number of conditioned locations successfully generated beyond training count)
S189.arch_detail: EDM2-based conditional diffusion models trained on CLEVR (Exp. 1/2/3 differ in labeling scheme); local patch-based intervention variants 2L/3L (grid_size 16, patch radius k=2); SDXL analyzed in pixel- and feature-space

S189.repr_analysis_finding: CLEVR models that succeed at length generalization exhibit local conditional scores; failing models (Exp. 2, 3) do not; explicitly enforcing local conditional scores (Exp. 2L, 3L) enables length generalization; SDXL pixel-space shows spatial locality but mostly absent conditional locality, with local conditional scores found in learned feature-space
S189.relevance_sigma_justification: Directly dissects the sigma-trap mechanism in conditional diffusion: proves an exact equivalence between a compositional structure (conditional projective composition) and local conditional scores, empirically shows that CLEVR models which succeed at length generalization exhibit local conditional scores while failing models do not, and demonstrates a causal architectural intervention that converts a failing model into a generalizing one; the locality analysis is a representation-level schema-coherence account of why compositional generalization fails.
S189.relevance_alignment_justification: No explicit discussion of AI safety or alignment; relevance is indirect: understanding the mechanisms by which generative models do or do not compose conditioners bears on reliable out-of-distribution behavior but the paper never frames this in alignment terms.
S189.other_metrics_reported: Kmax counts from automated classifier over 1024 samples; conditional-locality and pixel-locality gradient metrics (conditioner gradient magnitudes, gradient energy, 90% energy area); color-experiment manual counting over 64 samples with 25% success threshold

S192.arch_detail: NQG-T5: hybrid of high-precision grammar-based NQG (QCFG grammar induction) with pretrained T5 seq2seq; also evaluated standalone NQG and T5 (T5-Base; T5-3B on Spider-XSP); also applies new Template/TMCD/Length splits to GeoQuery and Spider
S192.train_data_note: Non-synthetic semantic parsing datasets: GeoQuery, Spider (SSP/XSP splits), plus synthetic SCAN; new template/TMCD/length train-test splits proposed; 51 databases in Spider
S192.relevance_sigma_justification: Systematically evaluates out-of-distribution compositional generalization of seq2seq semantic parsers on non-synthetic data via new template/TMCD/length splits, quantifies split difficulty with compound divergence and %ZA, and proposes a hybrid grammar+pretrained model to bridge the compositional generalization gap.
S192.relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; a semantic parsing benchmark and architecture study focused on compositional generalization and natural language variation.
S192.limitations_text: Evaluation restricted to semantic parsing datasets in English; NQG-T5 relies on computationally expensive pretrained T5 fine-tuning and inference (T5-3B especially); NQG limited by QCFG expressiveness and greedy grammar induction; QCFGs cannot represent semantic similarity or logical equivalence relations
S192.open_questions_text: Handling both OOD compositional generalization and natural language variation remains open; future work on alternative template/TMCD split construction, SemQL intermediate representations to increase source-target correspondence, and more flexible grammar learning/inference approaches
S192.other_metrics_reported: NQG coverage and precision per split; %ZA (test atoms unseen in training); error analysis via trigram language-model probability of first incorrect symbol

S193.title: Enhancing Compositional Generalization via Compositional Feature Alignment
S193.authors: Haoxiang Wang; Haozhe Si; Huajie Shao; Han Zhao
S193.task_custom_name: CG-Bench: compositional (unseen domain-class combination) splits of OfficeHome, DomainNet, iWildCam, FMoW
S193.ood_difficulty_metric_name: zero-shot accuracy of each domain-class combination (lowest 20% designated OOD set)
S193.arch_detail: Pretrained vision foundation models OpenAI CLIP ViT-B/16 and Meta DINOv2 ViT-B/14; finetuning: full FT, linear-probe-then-FT (LP-FT), reweighting, and CFA (two orthogonal linear heads with multi-label CE + orthogonality, frozen during stage-2 encoder finetuning); optional WiSE-FT interpolation
S193.train_data_note: CG-Bench derived from OfficeHome, DomainNet, iWildCam (WILDS), FMoW; E x K domain-class matrix masked so all rows/columns covered but some combinations unseen; ID train/val 9:1, OOD split into val/test
S193.train_regime_other: CFA two-stage finetuning: orthogonal class/domain linear heads with multi-label CE + L2 orthogonality (lambda=0 in stage 2), frozen heads during encoder finetuning; AdamW + cosine annealing
S193.schema_coherence_notes: No quantified coherence proxy; CFA imposes head orthogonality and is motivated theoretically via compositional feature learning, but no representation-level coherence metric is measured
S193.repr_analysis_finding: Feature visualization of CLIP ViT-B/16 encoder on DomainNet before vs after CFA finetuning shows the encoder learns compositionally structured features (class x domain)
S193.relevance_sigma_justification: Directly addresses compositional generalization failure as unseen domain-class combinations: builds CG-Bench from four real-world image datasets, shows CLIP/DINOv2 pretraining-finetuning struggles, and proposes Compositional Feature Alignment (orthogonal class/domain heads) with theoretical and empirical justification, reporting ID and OOD top-1 accuracy per method per dataset.
S193.relevance_alignment_justification: Relevant to alignment only through OOD/compositional robustness of foundation-model finetuning; the paper never discusses safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization.
S193.open_questions_text: Authors note a persistent ID-OOD performance gap, indicating compositional generalization remains challenging and needs future algorithm advancement.
S193.other_metrics_reported: F1-macro (ID and OOD); median/quantile test accuracy vs training data size (DomainNet); zero-shot accuracy distributions; feature visualizations

S197.title: Improving Compositional Generalization with Latent Structure and Data Augmentation
S197.authors: Linlu Qiu; Peter Shaw; Panupong Pasupat; Paweł Krzysztof Nowak; Tal Linzen; Fei Sha; Kristina Toutanova
S197.arch_detail: Pre-trained T5 seq2seq model fine-tuned on original plus CSL-sampled synthetic examples; CSL is a generative model with an induced quasi-synchronous context-free grammar (QCFG) backbone and a parametric state-cluster model; compared with NQG-T5, LeAR, GECA, SpanBasedSP, C2F
S197.train_data_note: SCAN, COGS, GeoQuery (template, TMCD, length splits), SMCalFlow-CS (8/16/32-shot compositional splits); T5 fine-tuned on original + CSL-sampled recombined examples
S197.augmentation_type: example recombination via induced generative grammar (CSL); compared with GECA recombination
S197.effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported; gains reported as accuracy points and relative improvements
S197.schema_coherence_notes: Compositional bias is transferred via training-data augmentation, not via representation-level coherence proxies; no probing/CKA/RSA-style analysis
S197.relevance_sigma_justification: Directly addresses out-of-distribution compositional generalization failure (the sigma-trap) with a data-augmentation solution: induces a compositional grammar (CSL) from training data and recombines examples to transfer compositional bias to T5, achieving new state-of-the-art on GeoQuery and SMCalFlow-CS compositional splits and nearly solving SCAN; relevance tempered by its focus on a specific augmentation method rather than training dynamics or a general theory of failure.
S197.relevance_alignment_justification: No direct connection to AI alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; indirect relevance through improving compositional generalization of deployed semantic parsing systems that must handle novel combinations in the wild.
S197.limitations_text: CSL grammars can lack coverage (e.g., %XCSL as low as 6.6% for SMCalFlow-CS 8-C); T5+CSL-Aug. is slightly worse than prior models on SMCalFlow-CS single-domain splits, attributed to inherent ambiguity in remaining errors; GECA can over-generate incorrect examples; CSL sampling may not be biased toward target-relevant examples; QCFG limitations analyzed in appendix.
S197.open_questions_text: Important direction: biasing CSL sampling towards examples most relevant to improving target-distribution performance; using pre-trained representations in CSL's parametric model; updating the parametric model with unlabeled target-distribution examples improves sample efficiency.
S197.other_metrics_reported: Grammar coverage (%XCSL); CSL eval-set coverage 99.9% on COGS vs 64.9% for NQG; 90%+ runtime decrease in grammar induction for GeoQuery

S201.arch_detail: Transformer encoder-decoder (3 encoder + 3 decoder layers) trained from scratch with task-conditioning (MT/SP patterns); subnetworks extracted via weight pruning (Cao et al. 2021) with ~50-70% unmasked weights per layer; causal concept-removal analyses per layer
S201.train_data_note: SLOG-style semantic parsing data with PP-SUBJ and PP-IOBJ generalization patterns; training on NVIDIA V100 GPUs (~300 hours total)
S201.train_regime_other: Transformer trained from scratch with task-conditioned patterns (MT/SP)

S201.schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy (probing, CKA, RSA) measured

S201.relevance_sigma_justification: Mechanistic dissection of the sigma-trap: causal analyses show the model depends on syntactic features yet its better-generalizing subnetwork implements a non-compositional algorithm acquired early in training, directly explaining why high benchmark scores can coexist with non-compositional competence.
S201.relevance_alignment_justification: Reveals that compositional competence on benchmarks can rest on non-compositional shortcuts acquired early in training, relevant to honest capability assessment, but with no explicit alignment or safety framing.

S203.ood_difficulty_metric_name: CLEVR-SYN easy/medium/hard: number of replaced unseen synonym concepts per program (1 / up to 3 / all)
S203.arch_detail: NeSyCoCo: LLM generates symbolic programs (dependency-augmented NL input), distributed word representations (GloVe-6B-300D, RoBERTa, SpaCy, one-hot tested) link linguistically motivated predicates to neural modules, soft composition of normalized predicate scores; baselines: MDETR, NSCL, LEFT, LLaVA, OpenFlamingo, ViperGPT, VisProg
S203.train_data_note: Trained with CLEVR programs (GT and LLM-generated); CLEVR-SYN built by replacing concepts in CLEVR validation programs with unseen synonyms via regex substitution
S203.train_regime_other: Neural module training with GT/LLM-generated programs; soft composition of normalized predicate scores; LLM program generation with syntactic parsing context
S203.effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported; ID-OOD gap visible across CLEVR (99.7) vs CLEVR-SYN (92.1/81.2/73.4) but not reported as a gap number
S203.schema_coherence_proxy_other: Pearson correlation (rho) between learned predicate scores of semantically similar (synonym) concepts; cosine similarity of predicate embeddings vs score correlation
S203.schema_coherence_notes: Per-pair rho values (Table 6): left/left-of 1.00, large/huge 0.97, front/front-of 0.98, small/little 0.91; weak for ball/sphere -0.02 and brown/chocolate 0.20. Embedding cosine similarity correlates with score correlation (Fig 5).
S203.repr_analysis_finding: Analysis of predicate-score space: substituted-concept scores correlate strongly with original predicate scores when embeddings are semantically close (cosine > 0.4); significant Pearson correlations (e.g., left/left-of p<0.01, large/huge p=0.01)
S203.relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets compositional generalization failure in vision-language reasoning: NeSyCoCo composes primitive concepts via differentiable soft composition of normalized predicate scores from LLM-generated symbolic programs, achieves SOTA on ReaSCAN and CLEVR-CoGenT, and measures zero-shot generalization to novel synonym concepts (CLEVR-SYN easy/medium/hard) with per-split accuracy.
S203.relevance_alignment_justification: Neuro-symbolic compositional reasoning for vision-language agents bears on robustness and interpretability relevant to AI safety, but the paper never discusses alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; relevance is indirect.
S203.limitations_text: Method struggles with semantically similar but context-sensitive predicates (e.g., ball/sphere, brown/chocolate) not fully captured by frozen embeddings; generalization depends on high-quality embeddings (cosine similarity above ~0.4); 5 CLEVR-Puzzle errors attributed to incorrect annotations.
S203.open_questions_text: Integrate NeSyCoCo into the DomiKnowS neuro-symbolic framework to make underlying neural models programmable instead of using a fixed neural architecture for predicates.
S203.other_metrics_reported: Pearson correlation (rho) and p-values of predicate-score substitutions; cosine similarity of predicate embeddings; language-encoder ablation (SpaCy, RoBERTa, one-hot, GloVe-6B-300D) on CLEVR and CLEVR-SYN Easy

S204.title: Compositional Generalization via Forced Rendering of Disentangled Latents
S204.authors: Qiyao Liang; Daoyuan Qian; Liu Ziyin; Ila Fiete
S204.task_custom_name: synthetic 2D Gaussian bump generation (decode (x,y) coordinates into spatial image)
S204.arch_detail: MLP decoder networks for coordinate-to-pixel generation; forced rendering via modular output-level embedding filters (one per disentangled input dimension) with low-rank regularization or factor-isolated data curation
S204.train_data_note: Synthetic 2D bump/stripe datasets parameterized by image size N (2N stripes + 0-50 bumps); data requirement scales linearly in N with stripes training vs ~N^3 for bumps-only
S204.effect_size_notes: No effect sizes; results reported as data-scaling thresholds to 90% target accuracy and representational volume metrics
S204.schema_coherence_notes: Volume metric (effective dimensionality of representation manifold) measured as a function of layer depth; representations remain smooth and uniform in OOD regions for the forced-rendering models, contrasting with re-entangling failure-mode models
S204.repr_analysis_finding: Networks that fail OOD extrapolation re-entangle factors in later layers via manifold warping (volume metric collapse, memorization via data superposition); successful forced-rendering networks show early-layer stripe scaffolds that localize into bumps in downstream layers, with uniform smooth OOD representations
S204.relevance_sigma_justification: Mechanistic analysis of why disentangled latents fail for compositional/OOD generalization (re-entanglement, manifold warping, memorization via superposition) plus an architectural/data intervention (forced rendering) that achieves zero-shot OOD composition; directly addresses the sigma-trap's compositional failure mechanism.
S204.relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; the work targets disentangled representation learning and compositional generalization on a toy generation task.
S204.limitations_text: Toy synthetic 2D bump setting limits scope; translation to large-scale models (diffusion, autoregressive, Transformers) and high-dimensional domains (vision, language) is an open next step; authors do not claim universal applicability and note interactive compositionality likely needs no one-size-fits-all solution.
S204.open_questions_text: Scaling the principles to standard disentanglement datasets and naturalistic settings; whether modular embedding and low-rank factorization constraints retain utility at scale; need for new metrics and frameworks for partial and hierarchical compositional structures.
S204.other_metrics_reported: Data-scaling thresholds to 90% accuracy on x/y coordinate generation as function of image size N; volume metric vs layer depth; neural tuning curves

sub_experiments.notes: No quantitative results in excerpt; data efficiency reported via scaling thresholds, not accuracies
