S206.title: The Impact of Depth on Compositional Generalization in Transformer Language Models
S206.authors: Jackson Petty; Sjoerd van Steenkiste; Ishita Dasgupta; Fei Sha; Dan Garrette; Tal Linzen
S206.arch_detail: Decoder-only transformer LMs in 3 equal-parameter size classes (41M/134M/374M); depth traded against width (feed-forward dim) to hold total params constant
S206.train_data_note: Pretrained as causal language models, fine-tuned on COGS, COGS-vf, GeoQuery, and English passivization task; depth-for-width tradeoff keeps parameters constant within size class
S206.effect_size_notes: No quantitative accuracy results in excerpt; relative depth-vs-generalization trends reported via figures
S206.schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy; singular-value rank analysis of feed-forward transforms performed (see repr_analysis), not a coherence score
S206.repr_analysis_finding: Rank analysis of feed-forward affine transforms: in deeper models transforms become increasingly skewed away from full rank use, with the image increasingly accounted for by the best i-rank approximations
S206.relevance_sigma_justification: Directly tests a structural cause of compositional generalization failure (sigma-trap): deeper decoder-only transformer LMs generalize more compositionally on COGS/COGS-vf/GeoQuery when depth is increased at constant parameter count, with benefits diminishing; but does not connect to training dynamics, flatness, or schema coherence.
S206.relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; purely an architectural investigation of compositional generalization in language models.
S206.limitations_text: Deepest models in each size class, far beyond the depth at which compositional generalization performance saturates, are not extensively explored; extreme feed-forward ratios degrade performance.
S206.other_metrics_reported: pretraining perplexity; in-distribution loss on fine-tuning tasks; training/inference latency (seconds per step)

sub_experiments.notes: No quantitative accuracies in excerpt; deeper models generalize more compositionally than shallower ones at equal params, single run per condition

S220.title: Swing-by Dynamics in Concept Learning and Compositional Generalization
S220.authors: Yongyi Yang; Core Francisco Park; Ekdeep Singh Lubana; Maya Okawa; Wei Hu; Hidenori Tanaka
S220.task_custom_name: SIM (structured identity mapping on Gaussian mixture with structured centroids)
S220.arch_detail: 2-layer symmetric linear model (theory); 2-layer MLP with linear or ReLU activations for SIM experiments; text-conditioned diffusion model for validation
S220.train_data_note: SIM: 5000 training samples per Gaussian cluster; d=64 by default; random rotation applied to train/test points; batch size 128, learning rate 0.1, 40 epochs
S220.effect_size_notes: No accuracies or effect sizes reported in excerpt; results are loss/weight learning-dynamics curves
S220.repr_analysis_finding: Tracks evolution of Jacobian entries (major/minor) over training: staged growth/suppression ('swing-by dynamics'); failure mode where a major entry is suppressed to 0 and the model is trapped generalizing only a subset of concepts, OOD loss converging to non-zero value
S220.relevance_sigma_justification: Theoretically characterizes compositional generalization learning dynamics on a simplified identity-mapping task: staged growth/suppression of Jacobian entries, nonmonotonic (multi-descent) loss, and failure modes where the model is trapped into generalizing only a subset of concepts and never fully generalizes OOD. Speaks directly to why compositional generalization fails, though on a simplified synthetic setup with validation on diffusion models.
S220.relevance_alignment_justification: No discussion of AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; contribution is a theoretical account of concept-learning dynamics in generative models.
S220.limitations_text: Theory relies on assumptions D.4/D.5 (small equal-weight initialization, sufficient signal-strength distinctions) whose breakdown leads to failure modes; analysis limited to 2-layer symmetric linear model without bias terms; generalization to deeper networks, ReLU, or NTK regime left open.
S220.open_questions_text: Systematically characterize behavior beyond the stated assumptions and conditions for OOD failure; generalize analysis to deep linear networks, two-layer ReLU networks, and NTK-regime models; investigate early-alignment of ReLU networks on the SIM task.

sub_experiments.notes: No accuracies reported; results are learning-dynamics curves (loss and Jacobian entries). Validation experiments use text-conditioned diffusion models; SIM experiments use 2-layer linear/ReLU MLPs, SGD batch 128, lr 0.1, 40 epochs.

S241.arch_detail: HierDiff: fine-tuned from Stable Diffusion v1.5 (U-Net) with frozen FLAN-T5-xl text encoder, time-dependent conditioning and sparsity regularization on attention maps; extended to 4.8B diffusion transformer (HierDiff-DiT)
S241.train_data_note: Fine-tuned on public LayoutSAM dataset (high-level text y + local descriptions); QWEN-v2.5 generates local descriptions at test time; DPG-Bench = 1,065 prompts; M=3 local concepts, lambda=1e-4
S241.effect_size_notes: No effect sizes; DPG-Bench composite and sub-metric scores with SDs over 3 seeds
S241.schema_coherence_proxy_other: cross-attention spatial overlap (sparsity surrogate for latent concept graph)
S241.schema_coherence_notes: Sparsity regularization Ln penalizes spatial overlap of cross-attention maps as a surrogate for a sparse latent graph; qualitative evidence only (Fig 6/7 show reduced overlap), no quantitative coherence values
S241.repr_analysis_finding: Cross-attention maps over diffusion steps: without sparsity constraint attention lumps objects together; with sparsity, overlapping areas reduce; time-dependent conditioning shifts attention from dispersed global to focused local across steps
S241.relevance_sigma_justification: Formalizes compositional generalization via causal modularity and minimal changes with an identifiability proof, operationalized as HierDiff, a T2I diffusion model whose hierarchical time-dependent conditioning and sparsity regularization improve composition on DPG-Bench (HierDiff 79.28 vs SD v1.5 63.18) - squarely addressing compositional failure (sigma-trap) from the generative-process side with theory grounding.
S241.relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; a causal-modularity theory and T2I generation method.
S241.limitations_text: Condition 3.3-iii assumes no direct causal influences among variables at each hierarchical level, which may restrict representative power; mitigation via additional hierarchical levels or more involved conditions.
S241.other_metrics_reported: DPG-Bench sub-metrics (Global/Entity/Attribute/Relation/Other); ablations w/o TD Global 85.15+/-2.26, w/o SR Global 83.09+/-2.49; Table 3 DPG scores for large DiT models (HierDiff-DiT 84.9)

S242.title: Provably Efficient Causal Model-Based Reinforcement Learning for Systematic Generalization
S242.authors: Mirco Mutti; Riccardo De Santi; Emanuele Rossi; Juan Felipe Calderon; Michael Bronstein; Marcello Restelli
S242.task_custom_name: systematic generalization in RL over feature-vector MDPs (synthetic person health/weight environment)
S242.arch_detail: Model-based RL agent: causal transition model estimated via causal structure estimation + Bayesian network estimation (independence tests, intersection of environment graphs), planning oracle on the learned model; no neural architectures involved
S242.train_data_note: Reward-free interactions from a subset of M environments (M=3 in validation); discrete variables with 3 values (0/1/2); synthetic environments represent person weight and academic performance influenced by training, sleep, study, diet, caffeine
S242.schema_coherence_notes: Learns the causal structure (dependency graph) of MDP transitions, but as a model-based RL objective, not a coherence probe of a neural representation
S242.relevance_sigma_justification: Provides a formal causal formulation of systematic generalization in sequential decision making, proves sample-complexity guarantees for generalization to unseen environments via a shared causal transition model, and identifies an inherent sub-optimality term when the model cannot fully explain new environment dynamics — directly relevant to the theory of compositional/OOD generalization failure.
S242.relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI alignment or safety; a theoretical RL generalization result with a toy personal-health validation, framing generalization as a sample-complexity question rather than a safety one.
S242.limitations_text: Systematic generalization is achieved only up to an unavoidable sub-optimality term related to lambda-sufficiency of the causal transition model; the error can only be overcome with additional interactions with the test MDP.
S242.other_metrics_reported: Graph edit distance between estimated and ground-truth causal structure; L1 distance between estimated and ground-truth causal transition model; results averaged over 10 repetitions with standard deviation

sub_experiments.notes: Synthetic validation: causal structure estimation (graph edit distance -> 0 with samples) and causal transition model estimation (L1 distance); 3 training environments, 10 repeats with avg +/- std, no accuracy values in text

S243.title: Compositional-ARC: Assessing Systematic Generalization in Abstract Spatial Reasoning
S243.authors: Philipp Mondorf; Shijia Zhou; Monica Riedler; Barbara Plank
S243.task_custom_name: Compositional-ARC (ARC-style abstract spatial reasoning; geometric transformation compositions)
S243.arch_detail: Small transformer encoder-decoder, 5.7M params, trained via meta-learning for compositionality (MLC); compared vs LLMs o3-mini, GPT-4o, Gemini 2.0 Flash, Llama-3.2-3B-ReARC and Mistral-NeMo-Minitron-8B (test-time training), and ARC-prize-2024 8B winner
S243.train_data_note: Compositional-ARC: 10x10 grids with colored objects; generalization from known transformations (translation, rotation) to novel combinations (translation+rotation); domain-specific LLMs use augmented inference (symmetries, color permutations) and one-epoch LoRA test-time training (r=64, alpha=16, 48 repeats, cosine LR 1e-4, warmup 0.25)
S243.effect_size_notes: No numeric results in excerpt; outcomes described qualitatively
S243.schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy measured in excerpt
S243.relevance_sigma_justification: Directly probes the sigma-trap: extends meta-learning for compositionality to abstract spatial reasoning, showing a 5.7M-param transformer systematically generalizes to unseen transformation combinations where SOTA LLMs fail and matches an 8B test-time-training ARC-prize model; but no analysis of training dynamics, flatness, or schema coherence.
S243.relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; a benchmark and generalization-capacity study.
S243.other_metrics_reported: color accuracy; shape accuracy; response-validity rates per model

S244.title: Impact of Pretraining Word Co-occurrence on Compositional Generalization in Multimodal Models
S244.task_custom_name: zero-shot ImageNet classification under concept-pair composition (GenPairs, ImageNet-Paste); VQA transfer (TextVQA, VQAv2)
S244.ood_difficulty_metric_name: pointwise mutual information (PMI) of concept pairs in pretraining captions
S244.arch_detail: CLIP ViT-B/32 pretrained on LAION-400M (primary); scaling: ViT-B/16+240, ViT-L/14, EVA01-g/14; LMMs built on CLIP for VQA transfer; images generated with Flux.1-dev (diffusion) and Llama 3.1 8B captions
S244.train_data_note: CLIP pretrained on LAION-400M (400M image-text pairs); fine-tuning on ImageNet classification with on-the-fly PMI-based edit augmentation
S244.augmentation_type: on-the-fly concept-pair pasting (PMI-based image edits) during CLIP fine-tuning
S244.effect_size_notes: Correlation between concept-pair PMI and CLIP zero-shot accuracy: r=0.97 (key concept pair) and r=0.99 (average PMI) on GenPairs; r=0.75 on ImageNet-Paste; r=0.70 TextVQA, r=0.62 VQAv2 for LMMs
S244.schema_coherence_notes: PMI is a data-level co-occurrence statistic, not a representation-level coherence proxy
S244.relevance_sigma_justification: Directly characterizes compositional generalization failure in multimodal models: shows CLIP zero-shot accuracy is governed by pretraining concept co-occurrence (PMI) rather than composition ability, quantifies the accuracy gap (18%/14% on synthetic, 10% on natural images), and shows PMI-based augmentation fine-tuning nearly eliminates it.
S244.relevance_alignment_justification: No AI safety, alignment, or goal-misgeneralization content; the paper is a pretraining-data analysis for understanding and improving compositional generalization in CLIP/LMMs.

S247.title: Latent Compositional Representations Improve Systematic Generalization in Grounded Question Answering
S247.authors: Ben Bogin; Sanjay Subramanian; Matt Gardner; Jonathan Berant
S247.task_custom_name: CLOSURE (grounded QA systematic generalization), CLEVR, CLEVR-Humans, synthetic arithmetic expressions (none in task vocabulary)
S247.arch_detail: GLT: CKY-style bottom-up parser computing representation and denotation for every question span, inducing latent trees from end-to-end (answer-only) supervision; modules include a VISUAL module; baselines: LSTM and Transformer seq2seq models
S247.train_data_note: CLOSURE systematic generalization benchmark for grounded QA over CLEVR-style scenes; arithmetic expressions setup also used
S247.effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported; comparison is qualitative (96.1% on CLOSURE vs prior models near-perfect on random ID split)
S247.schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy (probing/CKA/compositionality score); tree structure is architectural, not measured as a coherence metric
S247.repr_analysis_finding: Evaluates induced latent trees: constituent recall 81.6% (CLEVR) / 83.1% (CLOSURE), average object F1 95.9% (CLEVR) / 94.7% (CLOSURE); missed constituents mostly differed by an extra prefix (e.g., 'any tiny green objects' instead of 'tiny green objects'); human forward-prediction test shows denotation trees help humans predict correctness (p<0.05)
S247.relevance_sigma_justification: Directly addresses systematic (compositional) generalization failure in grounded QA: prior models near-perfect on random ID splits collapse on CLOSURE OOD compositions, while the latent-tree GLT reaches 96.1%, tying the sigma-trap to shortcut learning and global representations.
S247.relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; interpretability analysis targets human understanding of model predictions, not safety.
S247.limitations_extractor: No explicit limitations section in excerpt; conclusion notes the model is restricted to compositional computation
S247.open_questions_text: Investigate the structures revealed by the model in other grounded QA setups; allow the model freedom to incorporate non-compositional signals, which go hand in hand with compositional computation in natural language.
S247.other_metrics_reported: Intermediate-output metrics: constituent recall and average object F1 (see repr_analysis_finding); CLEVR (random split) accuracy 99.1%; arithmetic expressions benchmark setup; human forward-prediction study (20 participants, group A vs B)

sub_experiments.notes: CLOSURE systematic generalization; 96.1% vs prior models that almost perfectly solve the random in-distribution split; no SD/seeds reported
CLEVR random split accuracy 99.1%; no OOD accuracy reported for CLEVR; errors mostly due to less interpretable VISUAL module

S248.title: Measuring Systematic Generalization in Neural Proof Generation with Transformers
S248.authors: Nicolas Gontier; Koustuv Sinha; Siva Reddy; Christopher Pal
S248.task_custom_name: CLUTRR (logical reasoning over entity relations; natural language proof generation)
S248.arch_detail: Small TLM: 5 layers, 192 embedding dim, 768 mlp hidden, 3 attention heads, ~3M params, max length 1024; large TLM ~145M (20 layers, 768 emb, 12 heads); GPT2 ~125M from-scratch and fine-tuned; encoder-decoder 5+5 layers 5.22M params
S248.train_data_note: CLUTRR dataset; models trained on levels 2, 4, 6 only, evaluated on levels 2-10; stories in facts template (amt template for GPT2); proof settings: no-proof, short-proof, short-proof-reversed, long-proof, long-proof-reversed
S248.effect_size_notes: No effect sizes or significance tests; all accuracy results reported only in figures
S248.schema_coherence_notes: Generated proofs are tested for logical consistency (proof validity), reported in figures only; proof validity measured alongside answer accuracy
S248.relevance_sigma_justification: Measures systematic generalization in neural proof generation, showing length-generalization failure on longer-than-trained proof sequences, backward-chaining superiority, and better generalization without proof training - direct evidence on when and why compositional generalization fails in Transformers.
S248.relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; focuses on measuring systematic generalization in proof generation with Transformer language models.
S248.limitations_text: TLMs fail to generalize to unseen facts due to the combinatorially large entity-fact space in CLUTRR; encoder-decoder models are sensitive to training sequence length, failing in both extrapolation (levels 7-10) and interpolation (levels 3, 5); model size improves generalization only marginally.
S248.open_questions_text: Deeper inspection of TLMs' underlying internal reasoning strategies, which appear efficient but harder to interpret.
S248.other_metrics_reported: Proof validity (logical consistency) of generated proofs; answer accuracy per difficulty level 2-10 across proof settings (np, sp, spr, lp, lpr) and models (2.5M, 145M, GPT2 125M from-scratch/fine-tuned, s2s 5.22M)

sub_experiments.notes: No quantitative results in excerpt (figures only). Small TLM trained on levels 2/4/6; reversed short-proof and no-proof settings generalize best

S255.title: Rule Extrapolation in Language Models: A Study of Compositional Generalization on OOD Prompts
S255.authors: Anna Mészáros; Szilvia Ujváry; Wieland Brendel; Patrik Reizinger; Ferenc Huszár
S255.task_custom_name: rule extrapolation on formal languages (L1-L6 regular/context-free/context-sensitive grammars)
S255.arch_detail: Autoregressive LMs trained on formal languages defined by intersections of rules; architectures compared: Linear, LSTM, Mamba (state space model), Transformer (decoder-only), xLSTM; rule-following accuracy for ID and OOD (rule-violating) prompts
S255.train_data_note: Formal languages L1-L6 (e.g., anbn, Dyck, anbncn) generated by rule intersections; OOD prompts violate at least one rule (zero probability under training distribution); rule extrapolation = staying consistent with remaining rules

S255.relevance_sigma_justification: Core sigma-trap study: defines rule extrapolation - OOD compositional generalization on formal languages where prompts violate rules - empirically compares five architectures across grammar classes and proposes a Solomonoff-inspired normative theory of when rule extrapolation is rational.
S255.relevance_alignment_justification: No explicit alignment framing, but analyzes when LM OOD rule-following behavior is desirable/rational, which bears on reliability and specification-following of deployed language models; primary relevance remains compositional generalization.
S255.limitations_text: Human-machine comparison is only a small pilot study that provides intuition rather than a rigorous evaluation of human performance; authors emphasize this caveat for the human baseline results.
S255.open_questions_text: Rigorous evaluation of human performance on rule extrapolation is left for future work; normative theory is an uncomputable ideal (Solomonoff-style) intended as a guide for practical models.

S280.authors: Mohammad Beigi; Ming Jin; Junshan Zhang; Qifan Wang; Lifu Huang
S280.task_custom_name: RLHF reward hacking detection and mitigation across three hacking domains: chat sycophancy, length bias, and code gaming
S280.arch_detail: LLM policies (e.g., Llama-2-7b) trained with RLHF/PPO; ARA adds a Hacker policy, a latent-representation Auditor (5M-85M params), and AG-RLHF reward gating with severity gamma in [0,8]
S280.train_data_note: Training details not in excerpt; Auditor capacity ablated from 5M to 85M parameters

S280.repr_analysis_finding: tSNE of reward-model representations h_x,y for exploitative responses shows chat sycophancy and length bias occupy nearly identical regions while code gaming forms a distinct proximate cluster; Auditor detection transfer (0.55-0.77 AUC) mirrors this representational geometry
S280.relevance_sigma_justification: Concerns reward hacking via spurious correlations in reward models (shortcut learning), which is a misgeneralization phenomenon, and evaluates cross-domain generalization of hacking, detection, and mitigation; not about compositional generalization per se.
S280.relevance_alignment_justification: Directly targets reward hacking, a core alignment failure in which models exploit proxy-reward spurious correlations while violating human intent, including emergent cross-domain misalignment; proposes active detection and mitigation (ARA/AG-RLHF) and is explicitly framed as AI safety research with an impact statement on dual-use concerns.
S280.limitations_text: Cross-domain transfer to code gaming is limited (0.55-0.62 AUC), so mitigating code gaming likely requires dedicated training data; impact statement acknowledges the dual-use concern of the Hacker component discovering exploits.

S281.title: Probing the Probes: Methods and Metrics for Concept Alignment
S281.authors: Jacob Lysnæs-Larsen; Marte Eggen; Inga Strümke
S281.task_custom_name: Concept Activation Vector (CAV) probing of CNN vision models; concept classification on image concepts (horses, dogs, primates, buildings)
S281.arch_detail: CNN vision models (specific architecture unspecified); probing methods: Classifier-CAVs, Segmentation-CAVs, Combination-CAVs, Pattern-CAVs, translation-invariant (GAP) CAV variants; spatial linear attribution concept localization
S281.train_data_note: Concept datasets for CAV training (e.g., horse, dog, primate, building concepts); concept training data size varied to study alignment scaling; hard-accuracy test set replaces backgrounds with concept-free random images
S281.schema_coherence_notes: Paper's core is concept alignment via CAV linear probes; argues probe accuracy alone is an unreliable alignment measure (probes exploit spurious correlations); hard (worst-group) accuracy, segmentation score, and augmentation robustness proposed as alignment metrics; no numeric values in excerpt
S281.repr_analysis_finding: Probe classification accuracy is an unreliable measure of concept alignment; deliberately misaligned probes exploiting spurious correlations reach accuracy close to standard probes; translation-invariant (GAP) CAVs increase alignment; TCAV scores are highly dependent on the probed layer, with some late layers lacking spikes for dog classes
S281.relevance_sigma_justification: Tangentially relevant: probe accuracy can be inflated by spurious correlations, and the paper introduces hard accuracy (worst-group accuracy on background-randomized images) as an OOD-like robustness metric; however, the object of study is explainability probes rather than model compositional or OOD generalization.
S281.relevance_alignment_justification: Relevant to AI safety through interpretability: concept alignment of CAVs/TCAV is a mechanistic-interpretability tool used for model auditing, bias mitigation, and adversarial detection; the paper shows probe accuracy is an unreliable audit metric and proposes alignment-based evaluation, but does not connect to goal misgeneralization or safety.
S281.open_questions_text: Future work should investigate the extent to which CNNs encode the absolute position of features (concepts may be encoded at the channel level, in superposition, or using absolute positions), and tailor probes to both model architecture and concept nature.

sub_experiments.notes: No quantitative results in excerpt; methods paper on CAV concept alignment

S286.title: Neural Collapse Inspired Feature Alignment for Out-of-Distribution Generalization
S286.authors: Chen, Z.; Zhang, M.; Cui, S.; Li, H.; Niu, G.; Gong, M.; Zhang, C.; Zhang, K.
S286.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
S286.task_custom_name: Spurious-correlation OOD classification (ColoredMNIST, ColoredCOCO, COCOPlaces, NICO)
S286.arch_detail: Backbone architectures not specified in excerpt; method learns per-environment local models and applies semantic masks to inputs at pixel or feature level
S286.train_data_note: Three toy datasets (ColoredMNIST, ColoredCOCO, COCOPlaces) and one real dataset (NICO); samples partitioned into environments either by known labels or by learned local models with maximum-likelihood assignment
S286.schema_coherence_notes: Method enforces neural collapse to a simplex equiangular tight frame (ETF) on semantic-mask features as a training objective, but the excerpt reports no empirical measurement of a representation-level coherence proxy

S286.open_questions_text: Investigate more effective and efficient environment partitioning techniques; apply the method to other domains such as segmentation and few-shot spurious correlation issues.
